business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "India's first and largest power exchange": commenced operations 2008, CERC regulated, publicly listed 2017 on NSE and BSE; a "Nation wide, Automated and Transparent Trading Platform for Physical Delivery of Electricity, Renewables & Certificates", with State Advisory Committee membership of 13 SERCs and a board seat in the Association of Power Exchanges (APEX).
- Group framing of four venture platforms: IEX (Est. 2008, "India's Premier Power Exchange, 9,100+ Participants"), IGX (Est. 2020, "India's First, Only Natural Gas Exchange"), an I-REC issuer (Est. 2022, "India's only International REC (I-REC) issuer") and Indian Coal Exchange ("Incorporated in 2026").
- Penetration headroom is the core thesis: "Exchanges: still <10% of India's power volumes"; "Europe trade more than half of their power generation through power exchanges".
- Technology as the defence of share: "Technology Prowess Positions us to Retain Prominent Market Share, Even Under Coupled Scenario" - 72% of cleared volume in I-DAM contributed by members using Bidding APIs and 56% by members using Trade Reports APIs.
- Business model described as "18 years of deep relationships, API-led integration and a service model built around the customers" and an "Asset-light, high-margin platform" with "Strong free cash flow for diversification".

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Stated philosophy: "Compounding Shareholder Returns: High ROE, Consistent Dividend Payout", with an asset-light platform generating "Strong free cash flow for diversification".
- Dividend payout (INR Cr) of 187 (FY23), 223 (FY24), 268 (FY25) and 312 (FY26), with payout % to PAT shown at 64, 65, 65 and 66.
- Return on Equity (%) of 42 (FY23), 44 (FY24), 44 (FY25) and 43 (FY26); net worth (INR Cr) of 784, 948, 1,098 and 1,307 over the same years.
- Free cash flow is being redeployed into new exchange verticals (gas, coal, I-RECs, prospective minerals exchange and BESS) rather than into asset-heavy capex.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Market coupling - key regulatory overhang] CERC's order dated 23 July 2025 initiated implementation of Day-Ahead Market coupling from January 2026; IEX challenged it at APTEL on 28 August 2025; APTEL's 13 February 2026 order held that coupling cannot be implemented without regulations so IEX "is not an aggrieved party at this stage", with liberty to challenge the final regulations later; IEX filed a plea against the APTEL order in the Supreme Court and "our appeal has been admitted for hearing in this matter".
- [Market coupling - draft regulations] CERC issued Draft Regulations on 17 April 2026 proposing Grid India as the Market Coupling Operator; comments were invited till 5 June 2026 with a public hearing on 10 June 2026. IEX's objections include "Insignificant gains of coupling as per simulations of CERC & NLDC", process violation of PMR 2021 that "only sought to re-distribute market share of IEX", non-disclosure of the shadow pilot report, a July'25 order "tainted by insider trading allegations", and Grid-India as sole MCO being a "single point of failure" requiring a fall-back allowing power exchanges to carry out price discovery.
- [Policy pipeline] Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 and Draft Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2025 both point to market deepening - "Larger role for power exchanges", progressive introduction of forward/derivative contracts, open access expansion, India Energy Stack digital infrastructure and gradual lowering of market interventions as liquidity increases.
- [Storage as a new demand pool] CEA targets of 37 GW / 147 GWh BESS and 44 GW / 236 GWh PSP by FY32, Rs 9,160 Cr earmarked for BESS VGF schemes, and merchant standalone ESS tenders from ACME (Rajasthan, 3200 MWh), Juniper (Rajasthan, 500 MWh) and Adani (Gujarat, 3400 MWh); the deck claims "Rs. 4-5/kWh Arbitrage and 500+ Cycles/Year Make Exchange the Marketplace for Storage", with FY26 annual arbitrage of Rs 4.81/kWh over 545 cycles (2 hrs / 2 cycles per day) and Rs 4.63/kWh over 365 cycles (4 hrs / 1 cycle per day).
- [Sell-side liquidity] ~22 GW of FDRE projects awarded, where energy over-capacity of 40-45% during solar hours is expected to be sold on the exchange, and such tenders also allow buying from the green market at ~5% on an annual basis.
